## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The dominant macro narrative as of Sunday 24 May 2026 is a stagflationary tilt — energy price inflation from the Iran war is eroding real consumer purchasing power while simultaneously forcing central banks to contemplate further tightening rather than easing. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY as of April, well above the Fed's 2% target, while PPI sits at 2.66% MoM, signalling upstream pipeline pressures have not abated [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL]. The Federal Funds Effective Rate is at 3.64%, but markets are now pricing a meaningful probability of at least one 25bps hike by December, according to CME FedWatch data cited in reporting [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/gold-set-weekly-loss-oil-driven-inflation-fears-boost-rate-hike-bets].

The 10-year US Treasury yield closed at 4.57% and the 2-year at 4.08% as of 21 May, representing a modestly positive term spread that reflects markets pricing in prolonged higher-for-longer policy and a geopolitical risk premium on longer-dated debt [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10]. The 30-year yield has reportedly breached 5%, compounding fiscal sustainability concerns as the US deficit continues to widen [Source: https://www.icis.com/explore/resources/news/2026/05/21/11210020/icis-economic-outlook-high-crude-oil-rising-inflation-threaten-us-gdp-growth]. Rising bond yields are beginning to compete with equities for capital allocation, which Reuters flagged as a key risk for the week ahead [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/wall-st-week-ahead-soaring-stocks-could-face-rocky-patch-earnings-wind-down-2026-05-22/].

Despite these headwinds, equity markets have been remarkably resilient. The S&P 500 closed at 7,473.47 on Friday, up 0.37%, and is within striking distance of all-time highs, with technology stocks up 23% year-to-date [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/why-kevin-warsh-defy-trump-171921469.html]. UBS has raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 7,900 and JPMorgan Private Bank sees a path to 9,000 over the next 12 months, both driven by the AI supercycle narrative [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/ubs-lifts-sp-500-annual-forecast-robust-consumer-spending-ai-demand]. Q1 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth is running at nearly 29% YoY, with tech heavyweights delivering the bulk of outperformance [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/ubs-lifts-sp-500-annual-forecast-robust-consumer-spending-ai-demand].

The new Fed Chair Warsh faces a structurally difficult inaugural challenge: FOMC minutes from the April 28–29 meeting state that "a majority of participants highlighted that some policy firming would likely become appropriate if inflation were to continue to run persistently above 2 percent" [Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/05/21/why-kevin-warsh-will-have-to-defy-trump-on-interes/]. This directly contradicts President Trump's desire for rate cuts, setting up an acute tension between the executive and the independent central bank. The EU is reportedly bracing for a "dramatically" worse economic outlook as the Iran war weighs on European energy costs and growth [Source: https://www.ft.com/content/1588aee4-0d8e-4c44-b250-843ec015f1f6], while ADNOC has warned that Gulf oil disruptions could persist until 2027 [Source: https://oilprice.com/Energy/Crude-Oil/ADNOC-Warns-Gulf-Oil-Disruptions-Could-Last-Until-2027.html].

Key catalysts for the week ahead include core PCE data on Thursday, earnings from Marvell Technology, Dell Technologies, and Costco, and any developments in US–Iran negotiations. The interaction between oil prices, Treasury yields, and Fed communication will be the critical triangle to monitor [Source: https://www.investors.com/research/investing-action-plan/stock-market-week-ahead-marvell-dell-costco-earnings-fed-inflation-gauge/].
